subject: Post-call: performance KPI alignment & POC asks
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novatek.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance KPI alignment & POC asks

Thanks again for the time today — useful conversation. Below is a condensed note from our call + the asks we discussed so we have a mutual checklist before we scope a short POC. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described:
- Intermittent p95 spikes during customer-facing streaming sessions (audio->text + token streaming) causing degraded UX and session drops.
- High tail latency on cold-starts (KV cache warm-up) and spikes when concurrent sessions increase.
- Cost unpredictability with current autoscaling: sudden GPU spinups create throughput variance and long recovery windows.

Current stack (as described):
- Models: Llama2-13B quantized variants for customer chat flows.
- Serving: In-house Triton fronted by a microservice mesh on GKE (private clusters).
- Observability: Prometheus + traces (you mentioned a sample trace file).

Goals / success criteria you called out:
- p95 (end-to-end user-experienced latency) <= 150ms for short chat turns (~<40 tokens) under normal load.
- First-token time for streaming UX < 250ms for 95% of sessions.
- Sustained concurrency target: 200 concurrent active streams, burst to 500 for short windows (1–2 minutes).
- Predictable per-request cost with documented batch/caching strategy.

Proposed POC scope (what Redwood will validate):
1) Baseline capture of current p95/first-byte and concurrency behavior using your representative traces.
2) Controlled load tests (sustained and burst) against a quantized variant in our Dedicated-like environment.
3) Streaming UX validation: measure first-byte and inter-token gaps for typical prompt patterns.
4) Operational checklist: prefix/KV caching, batching settings, and recommended autoscale policy.

Immediate asks from Novatek to proceed:
- Share representative traces and any synthetic load scripts (you mentioned trace_0427.zip).
- Confirm a 1-week window for an isolated POC.
- List of security/compliance items we should be aware of for a private deployment.

Next steps (proposed):
- Redwood to draft a brief POC plan and cost estimate (we'll include the test scenarios and pass/fail criteria). Target to send by EOD Fri Apr 30.
- Tech deep-dive with Rishi and your infra lead to go through network/ingress and KV/cache behavior (30–45 minutes).
- Share the trace file and security questionnaire via your preferred channel.

I'll attach the initial POC checklist and a quick template for SLO targets.

— Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: redwood_poc_checklist.pdf (draft), security_questionnaire_2027.docx (template)

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novatek.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance KPI alignment & POC asks

Thanks Markus — appreciate the tidy summary. A few clarifications and additions from our side:

Clarifications:
- Our reported p95 spikes are most noticeable for streaming sessions that include an initial NLU pass + multi-turn back-and-forth; cold-start p95 has hit ~700–900ms in those cases, not the steady-state p95.
- Average token count per user turn is ~35–50 tokens; long sessions can go to 400+ tokens total across a session.

Additional context:
- Infra: GKE private clusters with node pools backed by A100 instances. We run Triton + a thin GRPC gateway.
- Model variants: two quantized variants in prod (8-bit weight-quantized Llama2-13B and a 4-bit trial variant). We suspect KV cache synchronization between nodes contributes to the first-token penalty.

I've uploaded the trace export and a filled-out security questionnaire to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-novatek-poc
Files:
- trace_0427.zip (sample traces from Fri Apr 23 stress window)
- security_questionnaire_2027.docx (completed to the extent we can share)

Agree on the POC approach. Prefer the POC week of May 10 — our infra lead (Asha Patel) is available then. Can Redwood provide a non-prod endpoint we can hit for the controlled test? Also please include an early estimate for cost per million tokens for the Dedicated-like environment so we can budget.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
VP of Product — Novatek Systems
sanjay@novatek.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novatek.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 12:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance KPI alignment & POC asks

@Sanjay thanks for the extra details — very helpful. From an engineering perspective here's a pragmatic POC checklist we can run through and what we'll measure: 

POC technical plan (summary):
- Test matrix: single-turn (<=40 tokens), short multi-turn (~150 tokens aggregated), long sessions (~400 tokens).
- Workloads: sustained concurrency at 200, burst ramps to 500 (30–120s), step-down to normal.
- Metrics we will capture: p50/p95/p99 latency end-to-end, first-byte latency for streaming, per-token throughput, GPU utilization, and KV cache miss rate.
- Config toggles to try: prefix/KV caching enabled, async cache warmers, small continuous batching (dynamic batch size up to 8), and quantization-aware kernels.

Immediate tech asks from Novatek so we can configure a representative baseline:
1) A short method to reproduce an end-to-end sample request (script or curl + sample payload).
2) A representative prompt set (5–10) with expected token lengths.
3) The trace_0427.zip (received) and any Grafana dashboards or Prometheus scrape targets we can mirror.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Redwood provides a non-prod endpoint and test harness by May 6.
- Joint testing during week of May 10 with Asha and your infra team.
- Results report with config recommendations and a cost-op estimate within 5 business days after tests.

I'll prepare the test harness and a short runbook. Attaching the internal POC checklist draft for our SREs to follow (redwood_poc_checklist.pdf).

— Rishi
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novatek.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance KPI alignment & POC asks

Great — thanks both. Sanjay, we'll plan to: 
- Provision a non-prod endpoint and a shared test harness by EOD May 6.
- Block a 45-minute tech kickoff (Rishi + Asha + 2 infra folks) on May 10. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm Asha's availability.
- Deliverable set after the run: performance report (p50/p95/p99), recommended cache/batching config, and a cost-per-token estimate for a Dedicated-like setup.

Can you share a quick SLO wishlist from your product team (even a one-liner per SLO) so we can bake it into the pass/fail criteria? Example placeholders: 
- "First token < 250ms for 95% of requests"
- "End-to-end p95 < 150ms for single-turn messages"

I'll attach the POC checklist and a short slide that explains how Redwood's prefix caching and smart batching reduce first-token and tail latencies. If the security questionnaire has items that block network access, note them in the Drive and we'll route them to our security contacts.

Looking forward — will follow up with the May 6 deliverables.

— Markus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: redwood_poc_checklist.pdf, security_questionnaire_2027.docx, trace_0427.zip
